title: Comparative study of adapting pre-trained models for driving behavior video captioning
abstract: arXiv:2609.39542v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: This report examines and compares some of the many fine tuning and prompting methods existing, applying them within the domain of autonomous driving. The idea is to compare these methods by adapting a Large Language Model (LLM) on a video dataset. LLM's have become extremely good at achieving a good understanding of different forms of data and this study aims to induce a low dimensional understanding of driving situations into our primary test model SpaceTimeGPT. Experiments on BDD-X (Berkeley DeepDrive eXplanation) dataset demonstrate good performance of the full fine tuning framework on some automatic metrics, and in some metrics, it even surpasses the baseline. We also try Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) and prompt engineering on VideoLLaVA model and discuss its limitations.

translated_title: 面向驾驶行为视频字幕生成的预训练模型适配方法比较研究
translated_abstract: 本报告考察并比较了现有的多种微调与提示方法，并将其应用于自动驾驶领域。其思路是通过在视频数据集上适配大语言模型（LLM）来比较这些方法。大语言模型在理解不同形式的数据方面已变得极为出色，本研究旨在将驾驶情境的低维理解注入我们的主要测试模型 SpaceTimeGPT 中。在 BDD-X（Berkeley DeepDrive eXplanation）数据集上的实验表明，全量微调框架在部分自动评估指标上表现良好，在某些指标上甚至超越了基线。我们还在 VideoLLaVA 模型上尝试了低秩适应（LoRA）和提示工程，并讨论了其局限性。
tldr: 本研究在自动驾驶视频字幕生成任务上比较了多种微调与提示方法，发现在 BDD-X 数据集上对 SpaceTimeGPT 进行全量微调表现最佳，部分指标甚至超越基线，而在 VideoLLaVA 上使用 LoRA 和提示工程则存在局限。
en_tdlr: This study compares fine-tuning and prompting methods for driving behavior video captioning, showing that full fine-tuning of SpaceTimeGPT on the BDD-X dataset achieves the best performance—surpassing the baseline on some metrics—while LoRA and prompt engineering on VideoLLaVA show limitations.
